summary.title: When life gives you lemons, write better error messages
summary.one_liner: Learn what makes an error message bad or good, and how Wix's cross-functional team audited and rewrote thousands of generic error messages.
keywords: how to write good error messages
takeaways: A good error message says what happened and why, and reassures users about what was not affected.
Avoid generic 'Something went wrong' text, technical jargon, blaming users or third parties, and a cutesy tone when stakes are high.
Give users a next step: a fix, a knowledge base link, or a way to contact Customer Care.
Wix found 7,643 error-related content keys, mapped each error in code with developers, and prioritized by frequency and whether it blocked the flow.
Error handling is a shared responsibility; Wix reviews errors one month after launch and lets UX writers challenge generic errors.
summary.summary: This Wix UX blog post describes a project that rewrote thousands of error messages across the Wix platform. It first defines bad traits (inappropriate tone, technical jargon, passing blame, unexplained generic messages) and good traits (saying what happened and why, reassurance, empathy, help to fix, and a way out via Customer Care). It then explains the process: searching the CMS for 7,643 error-related keys, having developers map each error in code, and having PMs, designers and writers propose fixes tracked on a Monday board. The post closes with lessons learned and process changes, such as a cross-functional error-handling team and a review one month after launch.
